description:
Confirmed via probe (bd:JMAP-tjvm.15 close comment): every workspace struct with a '#[serde(flatten)] pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>' field is vulnerable to silent spoofing — a caller can put a typed-field's wire name into 'extra' and the flatten will SHADOW the typed value at serialize time.

Probe results from EmailImportInput { blob_id: 'REAL', extra: {'blobId': 'SPOOF'} }:
  - serde_json::to_value() returns {'blobId': 'SPOOF', ...} (typed value LOST entirely)
  - serde_json::to_string() returns '{"blobId":"REAL",...,"blobId":"SPOOF"}' (duplicate keys; per RFC 8259 §4 server behavior is impl-defined; serde_json on the receiving side takes the last value = 'SPOOF')

Probe also confirmed for EmailGetParams: extras carrying 'fetchTextBodyValues' and 'maxBodyValueBytes' silently overrode the typed Some(false) and Some(1024) at to_value time.

JMAP-tjvm.1/.2 fix is INSUFFICIENT — that fix protected the args-level merge (entry().or_insert()), but the bug occurs INSIDE the params Serialize call where the flattened extras overwrite typed fields BEFORE the to_value Map is even built. The /1/2 args-level merge then sees the already-clobbered Map.

Affected types (every '#[serde(flatten)] extra: Map' in the workspace):
  - jmap-mail-client: EmailGetParams, EmailCopyParams, MailboxSetParams, EmailSubmissionSetParams, EmailImportInput, EmailParseParams (6)
  - jmap-calendars-client: CalendarEventGetParams, CalendarEventParseParams, PrincipalGetAvailabilityParams (3)
  - jmap-contacts-client: AddressBookSetParams (1)
  - jmap-filenode-client: FileNodeSetParams, FileNodeCopyParams (2)
  - jmap-metadata-client: Metadata{Get,Set,Changes,Query,QueryChanges}Params (5)
  - All *-types crates: every public data-object struct with the workspace extras-preservation extra field (Email, Mailbox, Thread, Calendar, etc.) — see workspace AGENTS.md 'Extras-preservation policy' in-scope list.

Threat model: a multi-tenant SaaS lets tenant A populate 'extra' from tenant input, and a trusted controller passes the 'real' typed field. Vendor-A's spoofed value wins at serialize time.

Fix-shape options (recommend B):

A. Custom Serialize impl per struct that strips reserved keys from 'extra' before emitting flatten. Maintenance burden: reserved-keys list per struct, stays in sync with typed fields.

B. Workspace helper proc-macro or build-time generated 'reserved_keys() -> &'static [&'static str]' on each struct that has the extras pattern. Generic Serialize wrapper or a 'sanitize_extras_for_serialize' helper. Cookie-cutter-friendly.

C. Validation at the call-site (reject inputs whose extras carry reserved keys). Lives in *-client handler code; requires per-method list. Doesn't help types-crate consumers (Email etc.) that serialize directly without going through a handler.

D. Drop the extras-preservation pattern entirely. Workspace just affirmed this pattern (JMAP-1j9k.9 closed 2026-05-17). Counter-policy — not viable.

Recommend B + audit: workspace-wide proc-macro to generate Serialize that filters extras before flatten, with a compile-time #[reserved(extras = [...])] attribute or similar.

P1: confirmed silent-spoof bug, but exploitation requires the specific multi-tenant trust split. Most callers in *typical* usage where the same trust boundary owns both typed args and extras are unaffected. Not P0 because no in-tree consumer demonstrates the vulnerable trust split; P1 because the bug is real and the fix is workspace-wide.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Workspace decision on fix shape (B vs A vs C).
2. Implementation in mail-client canonical first.
3. Cookie-cutter propagation across all extension-client crates and all type crates with the extras pattern.
4. Regression test pattern in mail-client showing 'extra cannot shadow typed field'.
title: Workspace sweep: filter reserved keys from #[serde(flatten)] extra Maps on all client/types *Params/*Input structs
